# 1 Enoch Chapter 56 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**1** There I saw the armies of the punishment-angels on the move, carrying iron and bronze rods.

**2** I asked the angel of peace who was with me, "Where are these going — the ones carrying those rods?" He answered, "To their chosen and beloved ones, to throw them into the pit of judgment in that valley."

**3** That valley will fill up with those chosen and beloved — their lives will end there, and the days they spent leading others astray will never be counted again.

**4** Then, in that era, the angels will turn and mass toward the east — toward the Parthians and the Medes. They will provoke the kings, stirring up a spirit of unrest, so that these kings will be driven from their thrones and burst out like lions from caves, like starving wolves among sheep.

**5** They will sweep up and trample the land of his chosen ones — his chosen people's land will become nothing more than a road and a threshing floor beneath them.

**6** But the city of my righteous ones will be a wall they cannot break through with their horses. Then they will turn on each other; each man's sword-arm will swing against his own kinsmen. A man will not recognize his brother, a son will not know his own father or mother — not until the bodies pile up beyond counting, and the punishment runs its full course.

**7** In those days Sheol will gape wide and swallow them whole, bringing their destruction to its end. Sheol will consume the sinners while the righteous watch.

**8** After this I saw another caravan — wagons full of men, with women riding alongside them, moving from west to east.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. The Parthian-Mede reference makes ch. 56 one of the most geopolitically specific chapters in the Parables. The self-destructive warfare of the invaders echoes Ezekiel 38:21 (Gog and Magog turning on each other).*
